solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Religious leader facing back of pulpit for natter

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader and teacher

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of pulpit is used

explanation.surface: A rabbi stands beside the pulpit, ready for a chat with the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just sets the two pieces side by side; the leader comes first, then T, the back of 'pulpit'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, a synonym of natter.

clue.text: Take on oxygen in publicity exercise

indicators.note: in places the element symbol within the publicity-plus-exercise pair

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a piece of publicity
PT is physical training, school exercise
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone takes on oxygen during a public fitness stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child, idea or role is to take it on as one's own, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Battle dress?

definitions.meaning: The 1854 Crimean War battle of the Charge of the Light Brigade
a woollen head covering, an item of clothing

explanation.definitionFit: The knitted helmet was named after the Crimean battle, where British troops wore such headgear.

clue.text: Bond's after drink and chicks

indicators.note: after places the bond piece behind the drink

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
a tie is a bond; the 's is 'is', linking to after

explanation.surface: James Bond, after a drink, eyes up some young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is simply a tie; 'chicks' is old slang for young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottie is British slang for attractive young women collectively, as is chicks.

clue.text: Leaves outside overdone soups

indicators.note: outside means the leaves piece surrounds the overdone piece

parts.note: the leaves of a book are its pages
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Salad leaves wrapped round soups that have been cooked too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' and 'soups' suggest the kitchen; the leaves are book pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is an old word for thick soup or stew, here in the plural.

clue.text: In stir prefer 'genial' criminal for bird

indicators.note: letters put in a stir are mixed up, so the quoted words are rearranged

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A convict in prison would rather the genial crook were a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like prison slang to match 'criminal', but here it signals the mixing of PREFER GENIAL into PEREGRINEFAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast raptor is a species of bird of prey.

clue.text: Show Elvis gyrating wearing casual shirt

indicators.note: the shirt is worn around the rearranged name, so it goes outside

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt, casual wear

indicators.note: gyrating, like Elvis's famous hips, signals the name's letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Elvis swivels his hips in a T-shirt on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gyrating' rearranges the singer's name, and 'wearing' has the casual shirt worn around those letters, the way a T-shirt goes round a body.
explanation.definitionFit: To televise something is to show it on television, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ace bottom in the air

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
the foot is the bottom of a page, bed or hill

explanation.surface: A top airman flies upside down with his bottom in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is about to happen, an idiom akin to being in the air.

clue.text: Uncertain note on Queen single's sung

parts.note: E is a musical note
I is the Roman numeral one, a single; the 's is 'is'
vocal music is sung

explanation.surface: A note about Queen's single being sung, perhaps in a music review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' and 'single' suggest the band and a record; 'on' puts E on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal means ambiguous or open to doubt, a synonym of uncertain.

clue.text: Security changing to all-clear

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Security staff switch the alert to all-clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan.

clue.text: Work on piano unveiling symphony initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A composer works at the piano, unveiling a new symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word but its O is the first initial.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, especially a numbered composition.

clue.text: Holding some ladies' underwear

definitions.meaning: a shop ... goods is holding them for sale
a nylon leg garment, a piece of women's hosiery

explanation.definitionFit: Stock means keep goods in store, and a stocking is also hosiery worn by women.

clue.text: Very old and tense, the compiler's dedicated

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the setter refers to themselves; the compiler's means I have, shortened to I've

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being very old, rather nervous, and devoted to their craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A votive offering is one dedicated in fulfilment of a vow, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: On reflection consumed fine cheese

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: consumed means ate
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, I ate some fine cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Enthusiastic English male that is not without love

parts.note: a bull is a male animal
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: without means the letter for love is dropped from not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An eager Englishman is described as anything but loveless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with energy and cheer, a synonym of enthusiastic.

clue.text: Cain sent wandering, for example

indicators.note: wandering signals the letters of the two words roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Cain was sent off to wander the land, as the Bible tells.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Cain is banished to wander as a fugitive, which makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' means for example, so the noun stands for an example.

clue.text: Soldier dropped in appropriate American gear

indicators.note: the paratrooper is dropped inside, fitting a soldier delivered by parachute

parts.note: apt means appropriate or fitting
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: A paratrooper drops in with suitable American kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment for a task, a synonym of gear.

clue.text: Old nuisance rising in crowd showing some bottle

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pair within the crowd

parts.note: a jam is a crush or crowd of people or cars

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome nuisance

explanation.surface: An old pest rises in a crowd showing off a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns OBORE into EROBO, which sits inside JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large wine bottle, holding about four standard bottles, so 'some bottle' indeed.

clue.text: African foreign national's in charge

indicators.note: in puts the nationals inside the charge

parts.note: to sue is to charge someone in court
Danes are nationals of Denmark, foreigners here; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An African visitor is now in charge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' is SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sudanese person is a native of Sudan, a country of Africa.

clue.text: Intimate with maiden's hand

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend, a pal
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A suitor becomes intimate with a young woman by taking her hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a young woman holding hands; it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the inner surface of the hand, a part standing for the whole.

clue.text: 'The Marksman' does for American actor!

definitions.meaning: Wesley ... is an American film actor

explanation.definitionFit: A sniper shoots from hiding, and Wesley Snipes starred in action films, giving both senses.

clue.text: Fate's woven threads, central character from mythology

parts.note: cloth is made of woven threads

indicators.note: the central character is the single middle letter of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: A Fate weaves threads, a key figure in Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Clotho is the Fate who spins the thread of life, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek mythology, the spinner.

clue.text: Occupied army on range

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ken is range of knowledge or sight

explanation.surface: An army has occupied a firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat that is taken is occupied, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Sailor certainly not right to knock back rum

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
no is an emphatic refusal

indicators.note: back means the knocking word is read in reverse

parts.note: to lam is to beat or knock hard

explanation.surface: A sailor definitely refuses to knock back his rum ration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back rum' suggests drinking; 'rum' is the definition, meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British slang for strange or odd, a synonym of abnormal.

clue.text: Opened one's eyes all right in terror

indicators.note: in puts the all-right piece inside the terror piece

parts.note: awe is dread or reverent fear
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone wakes with a start, relieved to be fine after a nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who woke opened their eyes from sleep, a phrase for the past tense verb.

clue.text: Aide's kept as retainer for bureau

indicators.note: the two words act as a retainer, holding the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: An aide is kept on as a retainer by a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' suggests a fee or servant, but it says the words retain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a writing desk with drawers, the furniture sense.

clue.text: Business takeover

definitions.meaning: one's business is one's job or trade
military ... is the seizure and control of territory

explanation.definitionFit: Occupation means a job, and also an invasion force's control of a country.

clue.text: One may fall for Brad Pitt

definitions.text: One may fall for Brad Pitt

parts.words: One may fall for Brad Pitt
parts.note: not a fan falling in love, but a double who takes falls in place of the film star

explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs dangerous scenes, such as falls, in place of an actor.

clue.text: Routine arrest following shaky case

indicators.note: following puts the arrest piece after the case
the case of a word is its outside pair of letters

parts.note: to stem a flow is to arrest it

explanation.surface: Police make a routine arrest after a shaky court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an established method or procedure, a synonym of routine.
